---
title: MCP server
description: Let a coding agent ask whether an AI system may ship, run evaluations and record evidence, without opening the app.
---

<Status state="shipped" />

`fairmind-mcp` serves nine tools over stdio. It is a thin layer over the [Python SDK](/docs/build/python-sdk) and reads the same environment variables.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_systems` | AI systems your key can see, with id, risk tier and lifecycle stage |
| `release_gate` | Verdict, confidence, the five checks and the reasons |
| `clause_map` | The gate per regulatory clause; optional `frameworks` such as `EUAIA` |
| `list_evaluations` | Searches the catalogue and says which evaluations FairMind can run |
| `describe_evaluation` | The files and parameters an evaluation takes, and whether it runs as a live behaviour test |
| `run_evaluation` | Runs on local files, against the live system (`live`) or on the connected agent platform (`use_connection`) |
| `run_fairness_test` | Uploads a local CSV, stores the measured result, returns metrics and the new gate |
| `record_monitoring_snapshot` | Compares recent decisions in a local CSV with the latest fairness run |
| `attest_check` | Records a person's statement that a check is satisfied |

Each tool returns a short text summary plus the full API response as structured content. File paths are paths on the machine running the server, normally yours.

<Steps>
<Step>
### Install

```bash
pip install fairmind-mcp        # or run it without installing: uvx fairmind-mcp
```

It is listed in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.adhit-r/fairmind`. To work on it from a checkout, run `uv sync` in `apps/mcp`.

The server targets the `mcp` 1.x `FastMCP` API (`mcp>=1.10,<2`).
</Step>

<Step>
### Set the environment

```bash
export FAIRMIND_API_URL=https://app.fairmind.xyz
export FAIRMIND_API_KEY=...
```

The client configurations below pass these through; none of them contains the key.
</Step>

<Step>
### Add it to your agent

<Tabs groupId="mcp-client" items={['Claude Code', '.mcp.json (per repository)', 'Claude Desktop']} persist>
<Tab value="Claude Code">
```bash
claude mcp add fairmind -- uvx fairmind-mcp
```
</Tab>
<Tab value=".mcp.json (per repository)">
```json title=".mcp.json"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairmind": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["fairmind-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "FAIRMIND_API_URL": "${FAIRMIND_API_URL}",
        "FAIRMIND_API_KEY": "${FAIRMIND_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Claude Desktop">
Desktop does not expand variables, so start the server through a shell:

```json title="claude_desktop_config.json"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairmind": {
      "command": "/bin/sh",
      "args": ["-c", "exec uvx fairmind-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Set the two variables in the environment that starts Claude Desktop, for example with `launchctl setenv` on macOS.
</Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
</Steps>

## Try it

- "May the credit-scoring system ship?" The agent calls `list_systems`, then `release_gate`.
- "Run the prompt injection tests on the support agent." It finds the evaluations, describes them and runs them.
- "Run a fairness test on `holdout.csv` for gender and region, outcome `repaid`, prediction `approved`." It calls `run_fairness_test` with the path on your machine.

<Callout type="warn" title="Attestations are statements">
`attest_check` writes evidence under your name. The tool tells the agent to use only statements you gave or confirmed, and the gate shows the check as attested, never proven.
</Callout>

Behaviour tests run as background jobs and can take minutes; `run_evaluation` waits for them. Set `FAIRMIND_ORG_ID` to act in an organisation other than the key's first.
